results.title: Off-Policy RL with Online Inference Tuning: My Solution to the CoRL 2026 RoboEval Challenge
results.snippet: The CoRL 2026 RoboEval challenge has eight bimanual tasks, and it ranks a policy not only on whether it succeeds but on how: every stage of the task, done safely, efficiently and with both arms in coordination, scored against human demonstrations. My solution has two parts. The generic part, carried over from my LeHome challenge solution, is off-policy RL on a $π_{0.5}$-based policy that is also its own value function. results.title: PlurVA-LLM-2026 Shared Task Track-1: Pluralistic Value Alignment in LLMs via Multilingual Fine-Tuning and Threshold Calibration
results.snippet: We present our system for the PlurVA-LLM 2026 Shared Task Track-1, which focuses on pluralistic value alignment in the contexts of China, Indonesia, and Sri Lanka. For this resource-constrained track, we fine-tuned Llama 3.1 8B Instruct using 4-bit QLoRA. Our approach combines option-permutation augmentation for Chinese data, annotator vote expansion for Indonesian data, and binary reformulation with SinhalaMMLU augmentation for Sri Lankan data. We further applied conditional threshold calibration to the predictions for the Sri Lankan data. The final system achieved accuracies of 0.785 for Ch…

results.title: Interpretable Preferences via Multi-Objective Reward Modeling and Mixture-of-Experts
results.snippet: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) has emerged as the primary method for aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences. The RLHF process typically starts by training a reward model (RM) using human preference data. Conventional RMs are trained on pairwise responses to the same user request, with relative ratings indicating which response humans prefer. The trained RM serves as a proxy for human preferences. However, due to the black-box nature of RMs, their outputs lack interpretability, as humans cannot intuitively understand why an RM thinks a response is good…

results.title: Overview of Dialogue Robot Competition 2022
results.snippet: Although many competitions have been held on dialogue systems in the past, no competition has been organized specifically for dialogue with humanoid robots. As the first such attempt in the world, we held a dialogue robot competition in 2020 to compare the performances of interactive robots using an android that closely resembles a human. Dialogue Robot Competition 2022 (DRC2022) was the second competition, held in August 2022. The task and regulations followed those of the first competition, while the evaluation method was improved and the event was internationalized. The competition has two…

results.title: The 4th Reactive Synthesis Competition (SYNTCOMP 2017): Benchmarks, Participants & Results
results.snippet: We report on the fourth reactive synthesis competition (SYNTCOMP 2017). We introduce two new benchmark classes that have been added to the SYNTCOMP library, and briefly describe the benchmark selection, evaluation scheme and the experimental setup of SYNTCOMP 2017. We present the participants of SYNTCOMP 2017, with a focus on changes with respect to the previous years and on the two completely new tools that have entered the competition. Finally, we present and analyze the results of our experimental evaluation, including a ranking of tools with respect to quantity and quality of solutions.

results.title: InfoRM: Mitigating Reward Hacking in RLHF via Information-Theoretic Reward Modeling
results.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37

findings.point: Dialogue Robot Competition 2022 (DRC2022) 是一个面向人形机器人对话系统的基准竞赛，包含预赛和决赛两轮，旨在评估交互式机器人的对话性能。
findings.evidence: DRC2022 为第二届对话机器人竞赛，首届于 2020 年举办。预赛有 12 支队伍参与，按实地实验方式评估对话机器人性能，选出 3 支队伍进入决赛。评估方法较首届有改进，并实现了国际化。
findings.attention: 中：作为首个专门针对人形机器人对话的竞赛，有一定领域关注度，但候选证据未提供引用数或后续影响力数据。
findings.recommendation: ★★★☆☆：提供了人形机器人对话评测的早期基准，但时效性较旧（2022），且未见后续版本或广泛采用证据。

findings.point: 第 4 届反应式综合竞赛 (SYNTCOMP 2017) 引入了两个新的基准类别，用于评估反应式综合工具的性能。
findings.evidence: SYNTCOMP 2017 新增两类基准到 SYNTCOMP 基准库，报告了基准选择、评估方案、实验设置及参赛者情况。属于形式化方法/综合领域竞赛，非直接面向具身智能或 VLA。
findings.attention: 低：属于形式化验证/综合领域，与具身智能/VLA/运动学/ROS2 关联度低，候选证据无引用数或社区热度信息。
findings.recommendation: ★★☆☆☆：与本主题相关性弱，仅作形式化方法基准参考。

findings.point: 多目标奖励建模结合专家混合 (MoE) 可提升 RLHF 中奖励模型的可解释性，旨在缓解奖励黑箱导致的奖励欺骗问题。
findings.evidence: 论文提出用多目标奖励建模 + MoE 构建可解释偏好模型，使奖励模型输出人类可理解，以保证决策过程与人类偏好一致。属于 LLM 对齐/RLHF 理论框架，非机器人学经典工作。
findings.attention: 中：RLHF 可解释性为热门方向，但候选证据未提供引用数或后续验证情况。
findings.recommendation: ★★★☆☆：提供 RLHF 奖励建模的新视角，若 VLA 引入 RLHF 微调可参考，但非机器人学核心理论。

findings.point: InfoRM 通过信息论视角的奖励建模缓解 RLHF 中的奖励欺骗，已在 NeurIPS 2023 (NeurIPS 37) 发表，引用数 9。
findings.evidence: InfoRM: Mitigating Reward Hacking in RLHF via Information-Theoretic Reward Modeling，发表于 Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37 (2024-01-01)，citations=9。属于 LLM 对齐理论贡献。
findings.attention: 中：顶会论文且有引用，但属于 LLM 对齐子领域，机器人学社区关注度需进一步核实。
findings.recommendation: ★★★★☆：权威会议发表、有引用支撑，理论扎实；若 VLA 采用 RLHF 微调可作为核心参考文献。

key_papers.why: NeurIPS 顶会论文，从信息论角度解决 RLHF 奖励欺骗，提供理论框架与实证验证，被引 9 次。
key_papers.attention: 中：顶会论文有引用，但属 LLM 对齐方向，机器人学直接关注度待核实。
key_papers.recommendation: ★★★★☆：理论贡献扎实，若研究 VLA 中的 RLHF 微调/奖励建模值得细读。

key_papers.why: 提出多目标奖励建模 + MoE 实现可解释偏好，针对 RLHF 奖励模型黑箱问题，为可解释对齐提供新范式。
key_papers.attention: 中：RLHF 可解释性为热点，但预印本尚无引用/复现证据。
key_papers.recommendation: ★★★☆☆：方法新颖，适合关注 RLHF 可解释性的研究者跟踪。

open_problems: 候选证据未覆盖具身智能/VLA/运动学/ROS2 领域的经典奠基性工作（如 RT-1/RT-2、Open X-Embodiment、LIBERO、SimplerEnv 等）、核心理论框架（如扩散策略、VLA 架构、动作分词器）及主流真机基准。需补充检索机器人学顶会 (CoRL/RSS/ICRA) 近 3 年论文与开源基准。
